Every text colour needs at least 4.5:1 on every background. The outline needs at least 3:1. The divider, a decorative line, needs at least 1.5:1 and less than the outline.
Six styles in the system font. Text grows with the font size setting.

Touch and hold a button to see it pressed. The buttons on this page do nothing when tapped.
The main action of a screen, such as Save. At most one on a screen.
An action that matters, but less than the main one. Not on sheets or dialogs, which use text buttons.
The quietest button: actions in dialogs, sheets, cards and lists.
A common action whose icon is clear on its own, such as search. TalkBack reads its label.
In an app it floats in the bottom end corner of the screen; here it sits in the page. It has no disabled state: when its action is not possible, the app leaves it out.
The one positive action a screen is for, such as adding a note. TalkBack reads its label.
The same, with text, when the icon alone is not clear. It can collapse to its icon while a list scrolls.
Chips are small and sit in groups. Only the chips under Try it do something when tapped.
Turns a filter on or off, such as Done above a list of tasks. A selected chip is filled and shows a check mark.
Starts a small, optional action related to the content near it, such as adding a reminder to a task.
Tap a field to focus it: its border and label turn the accent colour. Only the field under Try it takes typing.
Typing text, such as a name or an amount. The label sits above the field and TalkBack reads it with the field.
The whole row is the touch target, text included. Only the rows under Try it change when tapped.
An option in a form that is saved later, such as Remind me in a new task. Several can be checked.
A setting that takes effect at once. When on, it is filled and its thumb shows a check mark.
One choice out of a few, all shown. Exactly one is selected. TalkBack reads its place in the group.
TalkBack reads the label and the value in words, not a percentage. Only the slider under Try it moves.
Picking a value in a range, such as a daily goal. With steps, it snaps to whole values.
Touch and hold a tappable card to see it pressed. The cards and buttons on this page do nothing when tapped.
One item set apart from the things around it, such as a note. A tappable card is one button, so it holds no buttons of its own.
Touch and hold a tappable list item to see it pressed. Nothing on this page does anything when tapped.
One row in a list of things that look alike, such as tasks. A tappable row is one touch target, text included. A selected row is the one open beside the list; TalkBack reads it as selected.
The heading of a group, such as Today above a list of tasks. TalkBack reads it as a heading.
A thin line between groups, where space alone does not show where one ends. TalkBack skips it.
What a screen or a list shows in place of its content. In an app it fills that space; here it sits in the page. Only the switch and the button under Try it do something when tapped.
When there is nothing yet, such as before the first note. It says what is missing and what to do.
While content is on its way, when the wait is long enough to notice. TalkBack reads its text.
When content could not be shown. It says what went wrong in plain words, and how to try again.
Each top bar is drawn in a frame, as the top of a screen. The buttons on this page do nothing when tapped.
The title of a screen, Back when the screen was opened from another one, and up to three actions for the whole screen. TalkBack reads the title as a heading.

In a window narrower than 600\u00A0dp the destinations are a bar along the bottom. From 600\u00A0dp they are a rail along the side. Each sample is drawn in a frame, for one window width. Only the one under Try it does something when tapped.
Switching between the three to five main places of an app. TalkBack reads each destination as a tab, and whether it is selected.
Each sample is drawn in a frame that stands for a window. Only the one under Try it does something when tapped.
A list, and one item from it. In a window narrower than 840\u00A0dp the item opens in place of the list, with Back. From 840\u00A0dp it opens beside the list.
Two panes show only in a window at least 840\u00A0dp wide. Turn the phone sideways, or open this page on a tablet held sideways, to see them.
Each dialog is drawn in place, as it looks in its window. In an app it opens over the screen, which dims. Only the button under Try it does something when tapped.
A question to answer before going on, such as before deleting a note. TalkBack reads the title when it opens. A tap outside it or Back closes it.
Each sheet is drawn in place, as it looks when open. In an app it slides up over the screen, which dims. Only the button under Try it does something when tapped.
A few actions or a short form about what is on the screen, such as what to do with a note. A swipe down, a tap above it or Back closes it.
Each snackbar is drawn in place. In an app it shows at the bottom of the screen, above the floating action button, and goes away by itself. Only the button under Try it does something when tapped.
A short message about something that just happened, such as a deleted note, with at most one action, such as Undo. TalkBack reads it when it appears.
Each menu is drawn in place, as it looks when open. In an app it opens over the button that shows it. Only the top bar under Try it does something when tapped.
A short list of actions that opens from a button, such as More options in a top bar. TalkBack reads each row as a button.

Each date picker is drawn in place, as it looks in its window, on a month that does not change. In an app it opens over the screen, on the chosen date or on this month. You can tap the days of a sample; its buttons do nothing.
Choosing a day, such as when a task is due. The pencil switches to typing the date. TalkBack reads each day in full.

Each time picker is drawn in place, as it looks in its window. In an app it opens over the screen, and uses AM and PM or the 24-hour clock as the phone is set. Only the button under Try it does something when tapped.
Choosing a time of day, such as when a reminder rings. Type the hour and the minute with the number keyboard. A time that cannot be is refused with an error.
The screens of the recovery key that every app shares, from core/security. Each state shows with sample words. They are no real key, and nothing here makes or stores one. Back returns to this list.
